reason: The text portrays the elite (priests, Levites, and community leaders including Jeshua, Zerubbabel, and other heads of families) very favorably. They are depicted as organizers of religious and construction efforts who faithfully follow the Law of Moses, direct the rebuilding of the altar, oversee the Temple work, and lead the community in worship and celebration. While some elder priests and Levites weep upon seeing the foundation—comparing it to the original Temple—this is presented as an understandable emotional response, not as an unfavorable characterization. The passage culminates with the people shouting in great rejoicing, which reflects positively on the leadership.
